finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF: the POST parameter `feed` is passed unvalidated to file_get_contents(), which fetches any URL. That includes http://169.254.169.254/ and RFC-1918 hosts, and PHP stream wrappers such as file:// and ftp://. Only the response length is echoed back (line 13), so the request is semi-blind. It still allows internal port and host probing, metadata reachability checks, and size oracles. Redirects are followed by default. Severity is HIGH under the skill's Check 1 rules, or MEDIUM if the length-only response is weighed as blind SSRF.

trace.note: Handler entered on any POST that has `feed` set; no require_admin() call and no session check
$xml = file_get_contents($_POST['feed']); the URL goes to the sink directly with no parsing, scheme or host check
echo strlen($xml) returns the fetched body length, which gives the attacker an oracle for success, failure and size

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, no scheme restriction, no hostname parsing and no IP/CIDR blocking. require_admin() is defined at line 4 but not called on this path. No redirect or wrapper restrictions. allow_url_fopen is assumed enabled (PHP default). No egress controls are visible in the repo.

verdict.reason: import.php:11-13 passes $_POST['feed'] straight into file_get_contents() and echoes strlen(). session_start() at line 2 and the unused require_admin() at line 4 do not gate this path, and no allowlist, scheme check or host check exists, so the semi-blind SSRF is reachable unauthenticated.

finding.claim: Admin-gated SSRF: the POST parameter `set_webhook` is passed unvalidated to curl_init() and executed immediately with curl_exec(). Any admin can make the server request arbitrary URLs, including cloud metadata and internal RFC-1918 services. cURL supports gopher://, file:// and other schemes unless CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS is set, and none is set here. The response is discarded and the code echoes only "ok", so this is blind SSRF. Severity is MEDIUM: the endpoint is admin-only, but admin does not demonstrably imply OS-level access.
finding.sink: curl_exec($ch) on a handle created by curl_init($hook) at import.php:20-22

trace.note: curl_init($hook) sets the target URL from user input

finding.guards_checked: The only guard is require_admin() (import.php:4-9), which is an authentication gate and not a target allowlist. No scheme or host allowlist, no CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS or CURLOPT_REDIR_PROTOCOLS, and no IP blocking. CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION is not set, so cURL does not follow redirects, but the initial URL is still fully attacker-chosen. Admin-only webhook registration alone would be excluded under 'Do not flag'. Here the value is not stored but fetched immediately, and the skill's Check 7 note says to retain at MEDIUM.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin() at import.php:4-9 gates the path (403 unless $_SESSION['is_admin']). It is an auth gate, not a URL allowlist, so there is no target validation.
verdict.reason: The trace matches import.php:17-22, but $_POST['set_webhook'] reaches curl_exec at import.php:22 only after require_admin() at import.php:18, so an unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker cannot control it and the admin-only source fails the source check.
